title: Synesthesia: When Senses Cross Wires
question: Why do some brains blend senses that evolution kept separate—hearing colors, tasting shapes, seeing numbers as personalities?
summary: For roughly 1 in 25 people, the boundaries between senses are porous: a violin note might flash blue, the number 7 might always feel grumpy, Tuesday might taste like ripe bananas. Synesthesia offers a rare, involuntary window into how perception is actually built—not sensed passively, but constructed, connected, and far more negotiable than intuition suggests.
